newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Court overturns Manila Hotel sale to Malaysia firm.
newsitem.headline: Court overturns Manila Hotel sale to Malaysia firm.

text.p: The Philippine Supreme Court on Monday awarded the sale of the historic Manila Hotel to a Filipino company, throwing out the winning bid of Malaysia's Renong Berhad.
The Supreme Court ordered the Government Service and Insurance System (GSIS), the owners of the hotel, to sell the hotel to the Manila Prince Hotel Corporation.
The decision ends a court battle that began in October 1995 when Manila Prince, after losing its bid to buy 51 percent of the hotel, petitioned the Supreme Court.
Manila Prince said the hotel was part of the national heritage and should not be sold to a foreign entity.
Situated by Manila Bay, Manila Hotel is considered one of the great luxury heritage hotels in Asia and served as the U.S. military headquarters during World War Two.
Renong, along with its partner ITT Sheraton, a unit of the U.S. ITT Corp, had bid 673.20 million pesos, or 44 pesos per share, for a 51 percent stake in the hotel.
Manila Prince's losing bid was worth 636.174 million pesos, or 41.58 pesos per share.
Subsequently, Manila Prince offered to match Renong's bid of 44 pesos per share.
A 15-judge panel of the Supreme Court said in an 11-4 decision that the sale should be granted to Manila Prince to uphold a "Filipino First Policy" in the constitution.
"It should be stressed that while the Malaysian firm offered the highest bid, it is not yet the winning bidder," the decision said.

"Since the Filipino First Policy provision of the Constitution bestows preference on qualified Filipinos, the mere tending of the highest bid is not an assurance that the highest bidder will be declared the winning bidder," it said.

The decision to set aside the sale of a government asset after the bidding process has been completed is the latest in a series of troubled cases that have raised fears that foreign businessmen might be discouraged from investing in the country.

Last week, the Philippine Court of Appeals temporarily halted the privatisation of the Manila Waterworks and Sewerage System in response to a petition which questioned the government's authority to go ahead with the deal. The government had already announced the winners of the two concessions offered.
The petitioners said President Fidel Ramos' authority to privatise the utility had expired in 1995.
Earlier this year, Ramos ordered rebidding in the privatisation of a container terminal at Subic Port, north of Manila.
That contract was won by a unit of Hong Kong's Hutchison Whampoa, but it was set aside by Ramos after a local company, which lost the bidding, complained that it should have been the winner.

In 1995, a contract won by Hong Kong's Consolidated Electric Power Asia, then a unit of Hopewell Holdings, to build a 1,200 MW power station was set aside after it was found the company would use banned technology.
